analysis.title: Oil Products Tracker: Supply Weakness Likely to Linger into 2027
key_insights: Refined product prices have been volatile over the past month on threats of a US diesel export ban, G7 pledges to release government diesel stocks, continued Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries and a crude rally.

The global average crude freight rate reached a new high of $24/bbl in October. This squeezes net margins for refineries reliant on long-haul crude imports and gives some product tankers an incentive to carry crude, which reduces product shipping capacity.
GS reiterates its recommendation to be long 2027 European summer gasoline as a hedge against further geopolitical escalation, given a highly uncertain Mideast and Russia supply outlook.
High-frequency refined product inventories are low across major hubs, leaving limited buffers against more supply disruptions. US gasoline and diesel stocks are below the historical range.
China gasoline and diesel inventories are down 8% and 11% yoy respectively. Singapore middle distillates stocks are down 44% yoy.
ARA jet fuel stocks have resumed drawing over the past month and are down 56% yoy, as local refineries prioritize diesel output.
Persian Gulf refined products exports are recovering slowly, even though estimated crude exports are near their 2025 average.
Refinery outages in the Middle East are about 1.6mb/d above seasonal norms and Russian outages are 4.2mb/d above seasonal norms.

Ship-to-ship transfers that support crude flows are harder to replicate for products, because products are more flammable and vary more in specification. Larger crude cargoes also spread fixed security costs across more barrels.
Deferred maintenance is likely to prolong product supply weakness into 2027. Planned maintenance rises sharply in 2027Q2 after an unusually light fall 2026 season.

Planned global refinery maintenance is down 1.7mb/d (27%) yoy, largely because the US postponed maintenance. The expected 2027Q2 increase is most pronounced relative to seasonal norms in Asia ex-China, led by India and South Korea.
High maintenance in India and South Korea, both major product exporters, could reduce diesel and jet fuel exports in 2027Q2. Deferred maintenance also raises the risk of unplanned outages.
Global average retail fuel prices are elevated at about $223/bbl, up $10/bbl from a month ago, which weighs on demand. GS nowcasts put European oil demand and US gasoline demand down 2% yoy.
Jet fuel demand is soft. GS estimates November demand up only 73kb/d yoy and 3% below trend.
US and Europe wholesale jet fuel margins are $30/bbl above Asia levels, potentially reflecting higher freight rates and a slight increase in Chinese jet exports to the rest of Asia.
US refineries continue to prioritize diesel and jet production at the expense of gasoline.

sector_views.rationale: Supply stays tight into 2027 on refinery outages, low inventories and deferred maintenance, with elevated product risk premia.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Up $10/bbl from a month ago. Elevated retail prices weigh on gasoline and diesel demand.

macro_indicators.reading: $24/bbl in October (Exhibit 19 shows $22/bbl vs $4/bbl a year ago)
macro_indicators.interpretation: A new high. It squeezes net refining margins for long-haul crude importers and diverts product tankers to crude.
Stronger Western runs only partly offset Middle East and Russia losses.
Middle East and Russia outages outweigh below-normal Western maintenance.
Deferral raises the risk of unplanned outages and sets up a heavier 2027Q2.
Nowcast. High retail prices are cutting gasoline demand.

trade_ideas.rationale: A hedge against further geopolitical escalation given the uncertain Mideast and Russia supply outlook and low product inventories.

risk_factors: Further geopolitical escalation in the Mideast and Russia
Unplanned refinery outages, made more likely by deferred maintenance
Demand destruction from elevated retail fuel prices
Latest two weeks of refinery outage estimates are prone to upward revisions
charts_described: Exhibit 1: Estimated Persian Gulf crude exports have recovered close to 2025 levels while refined products exports remain low.
Exhibit 2: Global planned refinery maintenance will likely be especially elevated in 2027Q2 after a record-low fall maintenance season.
Exhibit 19: Global average crude freight rate surged to $22/bbl from $4/bbl a year ago.
Exhibit 23: Heavy distillates stocks in Fujairah stabilize at 57% lower than year-ago levels.
Exhibit 25: Jazan refinery (Saudi Arabia) restart date pushed back to end of October.
Exhibit 26: Maintenance at Saint John refinery (Canada) to reduce gasoline exports to the US Northeast by around 50kb/d.
